subject: HorizonMart service degradation — latency & error surge: RCA & exec readout
body:
From: Anya Gomez <anya@horizonmart.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: HorizonMart Oncall <oncall@horizonmart.com>
Date: Tue, 11 Jan 2028 09:04:00 -0800
Subject: Spike in latency & errors this morning — urgent

Karthik / team,

We saw a sustained latency spike across HorizonMart storefront between 06:15–08:40 PST this morning and a concurrent increase in 5xx errors for our checkout rerank route. Traffic profile was normal; CPU on our side was fine. Impact: 12% drop in conversion during the window.

Attached are the logs and a short timeline from our end. Please confirm whether this was on Redwood's serving plane and advise next steps — our execs are asking for an RCA and mitigation plan.

Thanks,
Anya
VP Product, HorizonMart

From: kimberly_park@redwood.ai <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Cc: grace_oconnor@redwood.ai, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 18 Jan 2028 11:12:00 -0800
Subject: Internal: RCA draft for HorizonMart — initial findings

Attaching RCA draft and three supporting artifacts (metrics CSV, KV cache heatmap, action register). Highlights from triage: 

1) Trigger & timeline:
- 06:12 PST: Small config push to serving pool B (non-customer-overlapping change) to update batching window alignment across models.
- 06:15–06:20: transient 95th latency increases observed across many customers; HorizonMart saw longest tail due to longer sequences and rerank calls.
- 06:24: autoscaler imbalance caused <10% of requests to be routed to a fallback pool with older quantized model variant that had a regression in per-token throughput for long sequences.
- 06:35–08:40: elevated error-rate (502/504) correlated with KV cache thrash and eviction storms for sequences >2048 tokens.

2) Root cause hypothesis:
- A concurrency bug in the continuous-batching scheduler caused mismatched batch shapes for long-sequence rerank requests when combined with a recent kernel selector heuristic. This produced pathologic memory thrash and KV cache eviction churn. When a small subset of requests were routed to the older fallback pool, that model variant's runtime suffered from a regression that amplified tail latency and errors.

3) Customer impact:
- HorizonMart: 06:15–08:40 PST — elevated latency, ~3% requests returned 5xx, 12% short-term conversion drop reported by customer.

4) Immediate mitigations performed:
- 06:30: Rollback of batching window alignment change (stopped further shape mismatches).
- 06:45: Hotfix to routing policy to avoid fallback pool for long-sequence reranks.
- 07:10: KV cache guard rails tightened to prevent full eviction storms.

5) Proposed corrective actions (short/medium term):
- Short (next 48h): Reproduce at scale in canary infra and add stricter batch-shape validation; create automatic guard that rejects mixing incompatible batch shapes.
- Medium (2–3 weeks): Harden kernel selector heuristics to prefer latency-stable kernels for long sequences and update quantized variant perf tests.
- Long (quarter): Capacity-modeled rollout policy for model variants with per-sequence-length SLAs; observability to tie per-model-version tail latency to rollout events.

6) Ask for exec involvement:
- Customer requests credit for conversion loss window and an executive readout. Grace, can you confirm horizonmart exec contact cadence?

Kim Park
Senior SRE, Redwood Inference

Attachments: HorizonMart-RCA-draft-20280120.pdf; prefix-kv-cache-metrics-20280110.csv; postmortem-action-register-20280127.xlsx

Subject: Re: Spike in latency & errors this morning — urgent

Anya — thanks for your patience. We've completed an initial RCA and attached a proposed remediation timeline. Key commitments: 
- We will run a targeted canary in your staging region within 48 hours and share results.
- We propose a one-time credit that covers the estimated conversion delta for the incident window; our finance team will draft the credit memo pending sign-off.
- We will deliver kernel-selector hardening and a rollback-safe rollout plan in the next 3 weeks.

We'd like to schedule a 30-min exec readout on Mon, Jan 23 at 10:00 PST to walk through findings and commitments. Does that time work for your team and HorizonMart execs?

Grace O'Connor
Account Lead, Redwood Inference

Folks,

Requesting approval for:
- A customer goodwill credit up to $55k (to be finalized by finance).
- Priority support for the three-week kernel-selector hardening sprint (assign two senior engineers).
- Exec readout on Mon Jan 23 10:00 PST (Grace to lead).

Please reply with ACK/NA or consult if the credit range needs escalation.

Vivek Kulkarni
VP, Customer Success — Redwood Inference

Grace / team — thanks for the RCA and the proposed timeline. Execs can make the Jan 23 slot — they've asked during the readout that Redwood provide:
- A concise one-page summary of root cause and mitigations (for our COO).
- The canary results and a post-canary checklist showing pass/fail criteria.
- Confirmation of the proposed credit and when we can expect the credit memo.

Appreciate the quickness here. We'll join the readout and circulation list.

Best,
Anya

Summary (for thread record):
- Incident window: 2028-01-11 06:15–08:40 PST — elevated latency and 5xx increase for long-sequence rerank calls.
- Root cause: batching scheduler mismatch + kernel-selector regression + fallback routing to regressed quantized model variant; KV cache eviction storms amplified errors.
- Short-term mitigations: rollback batching change, routing hotfix, KV guard rails.
- Commitments: 48h canary, 3-week kernel hardening sprint, finance to produce customer credit memo (estimate $55k).
- Next steps: Exec readout scheduled 2028-01-23 10:00 PST; post-canary report due 2028-01-25; action register closed by 2028-02-01.

Thread closed after action register sign-off.
